t.1.137.1: Then, when the night had passed, all the people of the city came there in haste, eager to see the sons of Pāṇḍu.
t.1.137.2: Then those people, extinguishing the blaze, saw that the house of lac had burned down, and the minister Purocana too.
t.1.137.3: "Surely this was contrived by Duryodhana, the doer of evil deeds, for the destruction of the Pāṇḍavas!" Thus the people cried out.
t.1.137.4: With Dhṛtarāṣṭra's knowledge, there is no doubt, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra has burned the heirs of Pāṇḍu, for he did not forbid him.
t.1.137.5: Surely Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, does not follow dharma, nor do Droṇa, Vidura, Kṛpa and the other Kauravas.
t.1.137.7: Then, as they cleared away the fire in search of the Pāṇḍavas, they saw the Niṣāda woman, burnt, blameless, with her five sons.
t.1.137.6: So we shall send word to the evil-minded Dhṛtarāṣṭra: “Your highest desire has been fulfilled; you have burned the Pāṇḍavas!”
t.1.137.8: But by that very digger, as he cleared the house, the tunnel was covered over with dust, unnoticed by those men.
t.1.137.10: But when King Dhṛtarāṣṭra heard that exceedingly unwelcome news, the destruction of the sons of Pāṇḍu, he lamented, deeply grieved.
t.1.137.9: Then those townspeople sent word to Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the Pāṇḍavas had been burned by the fire, and the minister Purocana as well.
t.1.137.11: Today King Pāṇḍu, my brother so hard to find, has died, now that those heroes have been burned together with their mother, most especially.
t.1.137.12: Let men go swiftly to the city of Vāraṇāvata; let them honor those heroes and her, the daughter of King Kunti.
t.1.137.14: Things having come to this, whatever beneficial rites I am able to have performed for the Pāṇḍavas and for Kuntī, let all that be done with wealth.
t.1.137.13: Let them have funeral rites performed, splendid and grand; and as for those who died there, let them honor their friends as well.
t.1.137.15: Having spoken thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, surrounded by his kinsmen, then performed the water-offering for the sons of Pāṇḍu.
t.1.137.16: All the Kauravas wailed loudly, utterly overcome with grief; but Vidura grieved only a little, for he knew the higher truth.
t.1.137.17: And the Pāṇḍavas too, O king, having gone out from the city of Vāraṇāvata, set out swiftly, making for the southern direction.
t.1.137.18: Having discerned the path by the stars in the night, O king, they faced southward and, striving onward, reached a dense forest.
t.1.137.19: Then the sons of Pāṇḍu, weary, tormented by thirst and blinded by sleep, again spoke these words to the mighty Bhīmasena.
t.1.137.20: What could be more painful than this, that we, in the dense forest, do not know the directions and are not even able to go on?
t.1.137.21: And we do not know whether that wicked Purocana has been burned. How then might we escape unnoticed from this danger?
t.1.137.23: Thus addressed by the King of Dharma, Bhīmasena of great strength took up Kuntī and his brothers, and the mighty one went forth swiftly.
t.1.137.22: Take us up once more and go on just as before, Bhārata, for you alone among us are strong, like the ever-moving wind.
